Alodia (founded 600) is the earliest of the four. Alodia, also known as Alwa (Greek: Ἀρούα, Aroua; Arabic: علوة, ʿAlwa), was a medieval kingdom in what is now central Sudan.

Seleucid Empire (founded 312 BC) is the earliest of the four.

Ghana Empire (founded 100) is the earliest of the four. It is uncertain among historians when Ghana's ruling dynasty began.

Kamakura shogunate (founded 1200) is the earliest of the four. The Kamakura shogunate (Japanese: 鎌倉幕府, Hepburn: Kamakura bakufu) was the feudal military government of Japan during the Kamakura period from 1185 to 1333.

Han dynasty (founded 206 BC) is the earliest of the four.
Scottish National Party (founded 1934) is the earliest of the four.

Kingdom of Kongo (founded 1395) is the earliest of the four. The Kingdom of Kongo (Kongo: Kongo Dya Ntotila or Wene wa Kongo; Portuguese: Reino do Congo; Latin: Regnum Congo) was a kingdom in Central Africa.
Numidia (founded 202 BC) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four came first?
Crown of Aragon (founded 1162) is the earliest of the four. The larger Crown of Aragon must not be confused with one of its constituent parts, the Kingdom of Aragon, from which it takes its name.
Which of these four began earliest?
Socialist Revolutionary Party (founded 1902) is the earliest of the four. The SRs were agrarian socialists and supporters of a democratic socialist Russian republic.
Which of these four is a monarch?
Sher Shah Suri is a monarch. The influence of his innovations and reforms extended far beyond his brief reign, being recognized as one of the greatest administrative rulers in India.
In what year was Indira Gandhi born?
Indira Gandhi: During her father Jawaharlal Nehru's premiership from 1947 to 1964, Gandhi was his hostess and accompanied him on his numerous foreign trips.
In what year was Edward VII born?
Edward VII: As Prince of Wales, Edward travelled throughout Britain performing ceremonial public duties and represented Britain on visits abroad.
In what year was Charles III born?
Charles III (Charles Philip Arthur George; born 14 November 1948) is King of the United Kingdom and the 14 other Commonwealth realms.
In what year was Prince Philip, Duke of Edinburgh born?
Prince Philip, Duke of Edinburgh: Philip was born in Greece into the Greek and Danish royal families.
In what year did Empress Elisabeth of Austria die?
Empress Elisabeth of Austria: Elisabeth was born into the Bavarian House of Wittelsbach but enjoyed an informal upbringing before marrying her first cousin, Emperor Franz Joseph I, at 16.
In what year did Golda Meir die?
Golda Meir (previously Meyerson; née Mabovitch; 3 May 1898 – 8 December 1978) was the prime minister of Israel from 1969 to 1974.
In what year did Qasem Soleimani die?
Qasem Soleimani: Former Mossad director Yossi Cohen said Soleimani's strategies had "personally tightened a noose around Israel's neck".
In what year was People's Party (Spain) founded?
People's Party (Spain): The People's Party was a 1989 re-foundation of People's Alliance (AP), a party led by former minister Manuel Fraga.
In what year was Timurid Empire founded?
Timurid Empire: The empire led to the Timurid Renaissance, particularly during the reign of astronomer and mathematician Ulugh Begh.
Rashidun Caliphate: Abu Bakr. The title Rashidun stems from the doctrine in Sunni Islam that the caliphs were "rightly guided".
Pahlavi dynasty: Reza Shah. The rest of the country was taken by 1923, and by October 1925 the Majlis agreed to depose and formally exile Ahmad Shah Qajar.
House of Habsburg: Guntram the Rich. The house takes its name from Habsburg Castle, a fortress built in the 1020s in present-day Switzerland by Radbot of Klettgau, who named his fortress Habsburg.
In which country is House of Tudor?
House of Tudor: Kingdom of England. The House of Tudor (TEW-dər) was an English and Welsh dynasty that held the throne of England from 1485 to 1603.
In which country is Second Chechen War?
Second Chechen War: Russia. Russian authorities were quick to blame Chechens for the bombings, although no Chechen, field commander or otherwise, took responsibility for the attacks.
In which country is Burning Man?
Burning Man: United States. Burning Man is a week-long large-scale desert event focused on "community, art, self-expression, and self-reliance" held annually in the Western United States.
In which country is Battle of Ilovaisk?
Battle of Ilovaisk: Ukraine. The Russian side opened fire on the evacuating Ukrainian soldiers, many of whom died whilst trying to escape.
In which country is Avignon Papacy?
Avignon Papacy: France. Clement refused to move to Rome, and in 1309 he moved his court to the papal enclave at Avignon, where it remained for the next 67 years.
In which country is History of New South Wales?

History of New South Wales: Australia. The history of New South Wales refers to the history of the Australian state of New South Wales and the area's preceding Indigenous and British colonial societies.
In which country did the Battle of Bunker Hill take place?
Battle of Bunker Hill: Thirteen Colonies. The Battle of Bunker Hill was fought on June 17, 1775, during the Siege of Boston in the first stage of the American Revolutionary War.
In which country did the Siege of Osaka take place?
Siege of Osaka: Japan. The siege put an end to the last major armed opposition to the establishment of the Tokugawa shogunate.
In which country is Yesh Atid based?
Yesh Atid: Israel. Yesh Atid (Hebrew: יֵשׁ עָתִיד, lit. 'There is a Future') is a centrist political party in Israel.
In which country is Battle of Warsaw (1920) based?
Battle of Warsaw (1920): Poland. After the Polish Kiev offensive, Soviet forces launched a successful counterattack in summer 1920, forcing the Polish army to retreat westward.
Which of these was an official language of the Byzantine Empire?
Byzantine Empire: medieval Latin. The term 'Byzantine Empire' was coined only after its demise; its citizens used the term 'Roman Empire' and called themselves 'Romans'.
Which of these was an official language of Great Moravia?
Great Moravia: Old Church Slavonic. The formations preceding it in these territories were Samo's tribal union (631–658) and the Pannonian Avar state (567–822).
Which of these was an official language of Bahmani Kingdom?
Bahmani Kingdom: Persian. The Bahmani Kingdom, or the Bahmani Sultanate, was a late medieval Persianate kingdom that ruled the Deccan Plateau in India.
Who is credited with discovering Permaculture?
Permaculture: Bill Mollison. Permaculture is an approach to land management and settlement design that adopts arrangements observed in flourishing natural ecosystems.

This political movement to end slavery gained major momentum in the western world during the late 1700s and 1800s, though France had briefly outlawed the practice as early as 1315 — what movement is it?
Abolitionism is the political movement to end slavery and liberate enslaved individuals around the world.

This Russian politician served as personal bodyguard to President Putin before rising to lead special forces that oversaw the 2014 annexation of Crimea, later becoming Deputy Defense Minister — who is he?
Aleksey Dyumin (born 28 August 1972) is a Russian politician serving as Secretary of the State Council since 2024.
Often called "The Father of the Philippine Revolution," this Filipino hero co-founded and led the secret society known as the Katipunan in its fight against Spanish colonial rule — who was he?
Andrés Bonifacio (November 30, 1863 - May 10, 1897) was a Filipino revolutionary leader.
Rising through Chile's army to General Chief of Staff, this officer toppled an elected president in 1973 and ran a military dictatorship for 17 years — who was he?
Augusto Pinochet (25 November 1915 - 10 December 2006) was a Chilean army officer and military dictator who ruled Chile from 1973 to 1990.
Nicknamed 'Bibi,' this MIT graduate and former Sayeret Matkal commando became his country's longest-serving prime minister. Who is he?
Benjamin Netanyahu (born 21 October 1949), nicknamed "Bibi", is an Israeli politician and diplomat who has served as Prime Minister of Israel since 2022.
A Methodist minister and theologian, he became Zimbabwe's first, ceremonial head of state in 1980 before Robert Mugabe succeeded him as executive president — who was he?
Canaan Banana (5 March 1936 - 10 November 2003) was a Zimbabwean Methodist minister, theologian, and politician who served as the first President of Zimbabwe from 1980 to 1987.
A U.S. senator from New York since 1999, this Democratic politician has led his party's Senate caucus since 2017, serving as both majority and minority leader at different points — who is he?
Chuck Schumer (born November 23, 1950) is an American politician serving since 1999 as a United States senator from New York.

Iceland's longest-serving prime minister, this former mayor of Reykjavík later chaired the Central Bank — only to face loud public demands for his resignation amid the 2008 financial crisis. Who was he?
Davíð Oddsson (17 January 1948 - 1 March 2026) was an Icelandic politician, and the longest-serving prime minister of Iceland, in office from 1991 to 2004.
Followers of this modern movement pick careers and donate to charities based on rigorous cost-benefit calculations, aiming to maximize positive impact worldwide — what movement is this?
Effective altruism (EA) is a 21st-century philosophical and social movement that advocates impartially calculating benefits and prioritizing causes to provide the greatest good.
On 30 April 1975, North Vietnamese forces under General Van Tien Dung captured South Vietnam's capital, triggering a frantic evacuation and ending the Vietnam War — what is this event called?

Fall of Saigon was captured by North Vietnam on 30 April 1975. The aftermath ushered in a transition period under the Provisional Revolutionary Government of the Republic of South Vietnam until the formal reunification in 1976.

This Indonesian politician governed Central Java for a decade before finishing third in the 2024 presidential race, having earlier spent two terms as a national legislator representing the same province — who is he?
Ganjar Pranowo (born 28 October 1968) is an Indonesian politician who served as the governor of Central Java between 2013 and 2023.

This Russian mystic and faith healer gained enormous influence over the imperial family of Tsar Nicholas II in the final years of the empire. Born a Siberian peasant in 1869, he's best remembered for his mysterious sway over the fate of Russia itself — who is this controversial figure?
Grigori Rasputin was Russian mystic (1869–1916). Grigori Yefimovich Rasputin (21 January [O.S. 9 January] 1869 – 30 December [O.S. 17 December] 1916) was a Russian mystic and faith healer.
Mother of two future English kings, this queen consort fled to her home country during the English Civil War in 1644, only to be left impoverished after her husband's execution — who is she?
Henrietta Maria of France (25 November 1609 - 10 September 1669) was Queen of England, Scotland and Ireland from her marriage to King Charles I on 13 June 1625 until his execution on 30 January 1649.
After serving as the 29th chief of Turkey's General Staff, this general won a parliamentary seat for Kayseri in 2023 — who is he?
Hulusi Akar (born 12 March 1952) is a retired four-star Turkish Armed Forces general who served as the Minister of National Defense from 2018 to 2023.
The eldest son of a former U.S. president and first lady, this businessman and environmentalist ran as the Democratic nominee in Nevada's 2006 Senate election — who is he?
Jack Carter (politician) (born July 3, 1947) is an American businessman, politician and environmentalist.
This biblical queen, wife of King Ahab of Israel, was thrown from a window on the orders of Jehu and devoured by dogs, as the prophet Elijah had foretold — who was she?
Jezebel was the daughter of Ithobaal I of Tyre and the wife of Ahab, King of Israel, according to the Book of Kings of the Hebrew Bible (1 Kings 16).
Born in Wales and raised in Adelaide, this Labor politician became the first and only woman to serve as both deputy prime minister and prime minister of Australia — who is she?
Julia Gillard (born 29 September 1961) is an Australian former politician who served as the 27th prime minister of Australia from 2010 to 2013.
Founded around 1399 in southern India, this geopolitical realm eventually became a British princely state from 1799 to 1947, persisting until 1950. What was it?
Kingdom of Mysore was a geopolitical realm in southern India founded in around 1399 in the vicinity of the modern-day city of Mysuru and prevailed until 1950.
This Chinese aerospace engineer spent 31 years at a satellite launch center before becoming his country's Minister of National Defense for just seven months in 2023 — who is he?
Li Shangfu (pinyin: L Shngf; born February 1958) is a Chinese aerospace engineer and former military administrator.
The Sanskrit word for 'human' literally means 'child of' this figure, an archetypal first man in Hindu tradition also considered the progenitor of humanity — who is he?
Manu (Hinduism) is a term found with various meanings in Hinduism.

This civil rights activist became the NAACP's first field secretary in Mississippi, working to desegregate the University of Mississippi and expand Black voting rights before his 1963 assassination — who was he?
Medgar Evers (July 2, 1925 - June 12, 1963) was an American civil rights activist who was the NAACP's first field secretary in Mississippi.
The final ruler of Iran until 1979, he took the title 'King of Kings' in 1967 and held others including 'Light of the Aryans.' Who was he?
Mohammad Reza Pahlavi (26 October 1919 - 27 July 1980) was the last Shah of Iran from 1941 to 1979.

Launched in 2017 by Crown Prince Mohammad bin Salman at the northern tip of the Red Sea, this 26,500-square-kilometer megaproject was widely mocked as unrealistic before being scaled way back. What is it?
Neom is a megaproject in Tabuk Province in Saudi Arabia.
A member of the Bundestag since 2006 representing Hesse, this German-Iranian politician co-led Alliance 90/The Greens with Ricarda Lang and now serves as Vice President of the Bundestag — who is he?
Omid Nouripour (born 18 June 1975) is a German-Iranian politician who has been serving as Vice President of the Bundestag since 2025.
This Finnish politician has led his country's National Coalition Party since 2016, and became prime minister of Finland in 2023 after previously serving as finance minister — who is he?
Grand Duke Michael Alexandrovich of Russia
Petteri Orpo (born 3 November 1969) is a Finnish politician currently serving as the prime minister of Finland since 2023.
A democratic socialist economist, this Ecuadorian served as his country's 45th president from 2007 to 2017 and has lived in Belgium since leaving office — who is he?
Rafael Correa (Spanish; born 6 April 1963) is an Ecuadorian politician and economist who served as the 45th president of Ecuador from 2007 to 2017.
First elected to a European legislature in 2013, this Maltese politician rose to become the first female president of that body since 2002 — who is she?
Roberta Metsola (ne Tedesco Triccas; born 18 January 1979) is a Maltese politician who has served as the president of the European Parliament since January 2022.
This Turkmen leader gave himself the title 'Türkmenbaşy' — Leader of all Turkmen — and ruled from the Soviet era until his death in 2006; who was he?
Saparmurat Niyazov (19 February 1940 - 21 December 2006) was a Turkmen politician and dictator who led Turkmenistan from 1985 until his death in 2006.
This Indian actress won acclaim for playing Tulsi Virani in a hit soap opera before pivoting to politics as a Bharatiya Janata Party leader who has held several Union Cabinet posts — who is she?
Smriti Irani (ne Malhotra; born 23 March 1976) is an Indian actress, politician, fashion model, and television producer.
This American politician has served as junior U.S. senator from Texas since 2013, after earlier serving as the state's solicitor general and later chairing the Senate Commerce Committee — who is he?
Ted Cruz (born December 22, 1970) is an American politician and attorney serving as the junior United States senator from Texas since 2013.

Tracing its roots to Radical Protestantism and Restorationism, this creedless faith tradition blends influences from Buddhism, Hinduism, Judaism and beyond under shared covenants of love — which tradition is this?
Unitarian Universalism (UUism or UU) is a liberal religious tradition characterized by its commitment to theological diversity, inclusivity, and social justice.

Married to Puyi, the last emperor of China, in 1922, this Manchu noblewoman later became empress consort of the Japanese puppet state of Manchukuo from 1934 until its monarchy was abolished in 1945 — name this empress?
Wanrong (13 November 1906 - 20 June 1946), of the Manchu Plain White Banner Gobulo clan, was the wife and empress consort of Puyi, the last emperor of China.
This Korean admiral is remembered for winning every one of at least 23 naval battles he fought against the Japanese navy during a 16th-century war — who was he?
Yi Sun-sin (Korean; April 28, 1545 - December 16, 1598) was a Korean admiral and military general known for his victories against the Japanese navy during the Imjin War in the Joseon period.
As head of the presidential guard, this officer overthrew Niger's president in a 2023 coup and was formally inaugurated as president two years later. Who is he?
Abdourahamane Tchiani: President of Niger since 2025.
Nearly blind and a quadriplegic reliant on a wheelchair after a teenage sporting accident, this imam founded and led an Islamist organization until his 2004 assassination — who was he?
Ahmed Yassin: Palestinian political and religious leader (1936–2004)
His simultaneous election as Prince of both Moldavia and Wallachia in 1859 effectively united the two states — making which liberal reformer the first domnitor of the Romanian Principalities?
Alexandru Ioan Cuza: First ruler of the United Principalities of Moldavia and Wallachia (1820–1873)

Mentioned on the Merneptah Stele around 1208 BCE, these two neighboring Iron Age kingdoms in the Southern Levant were said to have once been united under kings Saul, David, and Solomon — what are they?
Ancient Israel and Judah: Near Eastern civilization during the Iron Age.
Son of Zeus and Hera and brother to strategy-minded Athena, which Olympian embodied war's raw brutality and bloodlust rather than tactics?
Ares: God of war in ancient Greek religion.

A Sunni Muslim Kurdish dynasty that founded the medieval Sultanate of Egypt in 1171 under Saladin, who abolished the Fatimid Caliphate after originally serving the Zengid ruler Nur al-Din. What dynasty was this?
Ayyubid dynasty: Sultanate in Egypt and Levant from 1171 to 1341.

This Ottoman sultan ruled from 1481 to 1512, welcomed Sephardi Jews expelled from Spain following the 1492 Alhambra Decree, and eventually abdicated his throne to his son, Selim I. Which sultan is this?
Bayezid II: Sultan of the Ottoman Empire from 1481 to 1512. Bayezid; 3 December 1447/1448 – 26 May 1512) was the sultan of the Ottoman Empire from 1481 to 1512.
This accountant-turned-politician served as governor of Lagos State before becoming Nigeria's 16th president in 2023, having earlier gone into exile under military ruler Sani Abacha — who is he?
Bola Tinubu: President of Nigeria since 2023. Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Adekunle Tinubu (born 29 March 1952) is a Nigerian politician serving as the 16th and current president of Nigeria since 2023.

This German jurist joined the Nazi Party in 1933 and used his legal theories to provide ideological justification for the regime, though he fell out of favor with senior officials by 1936 — who is he?
Carl Schmitt: German jurist and political theorist (1888–1985)
Born into a German duchy and married to King George III, this queen served an astonishing 57 years as Britain's longest-serving queen consort and also became Queen of Hanover. Who was she?
Charlotte of Mecklenburg-Strelitz: Queen of Great Britain and Ireland from 1761 to 1818.
Taking its name from the Latin for 'common,' this ideology imagines a society with no private property, no social classes, and ultimately no money or state at all — what is it?
Taking office at age 35, this president became his country's youngest elected leader after Ecuador's National Assembly was dissolved via a constitutional mechanism in 2023 — who is he?
Daniel Noboa: President of Ecuador since 2023. Before his political career, Noboa served in several positions at Noboa Corporation, an exporting business founded by his grandfather.
The first woman to become president of Peru, she took office in December 2022 after her predecessor's failed attempt to dissolve Congress, and was herself removed from power in 2025 — who is she?
Dina Boluarte: President of Peru from 2022 to 2025. Boluarte aligned herself with the right-wing majority of the Peruvian Congress, and received support from the Peruvian Armed Forces.
Alongside Tenzing Norgay, this New Zealand mountaineer became one of the first two people confirmed to reach the top of Mount Everest, on 29 May 1953 — who is he?
Selected in 1866 to marry the future King Gojong, this consort — known in her lifetime as Queen Min — saw her own clan push the regent, her father-in-law, out of power. Who was she?
Empress Myeongseong: Regent of Joseon from 1873 to 1895.
Aided by his interpreter La Malinche and thousands of Tlaxcaltec allies, Hernán Cortés ended the Aztec civilization with this 1521 siege — what's the event called?
Fall of Tenochtitlan: 1521 conquest of the Aztec capital by the Spanish Empire and rival indigenous tribes.

Sparked partly by the 'Ems dispatch' after a Hohenzollern prince's bid for the Spanish throne collapsed, this 1870-71 conflict pitted France against a German confederation led by Otto von Bismarck — which conflict?
Known in early Welsh sources by the name Gwalchmei, this Knight of the Round Table stars in a Middle English poem pitting him against a mysterious green-clad challenger — who is he?

Rising to prominence during Greece's government-debt crisis, this far-right, neo-Nazi organization became the third-largest party in the Greek parliament following the January 2015 election, before its support collapsed — which group?
Golden Dawn (Greece): Greek neo-Nazi criminal organisation.
Serving as both his country's first prime minister and later its third president, this Namibian leader also chaired the Southern African Development Community starting in 2018 — who is he?
Hage Geingob: President of Namibia from 2015 to 2024.
Said to be a daughter of Loki, this Norse underworld ruler was appointed by Odin to preside over a shadowy realm in Niflheim, where she receives a portion of the dead — who is she?
Hel (mythological being): Underworld entity in Norse mythology.

This German banker headed the Reichsbank in both the Weimar Republic and the early Nazi era, and helped persuade Hindenburg to appoint Hitler's first government despite later opposing some rearmament policies — who is he?
Hjalmar Schacht: German politician, banker, and economist (1877–1970)
Dictating an account titled 'A Gift to Those Who Contemplate the Wonders of Cities,' this 14th-century Tangier-born traveler covered roughly 117,000 km — more than Marco Polo or Zheng He — who is he?
Ibn Battuta: Maghrebi traveller and scholar (1304–1368/1369)
In this Islamic narration, Muhammad makes a night journey and ascends to the sky, glimpsing the afterlife before returning — alluded to in Surah al-Isra. What is it called?
Signs of the coming of Judgement Day
Isra' and Mi'raj: Journey by Muhammad in Islamic tradition.

A follower of a controversial Bohemian religious reformer, this Czech military leader led Hussite forces to victory against three separate crusades and was never defeated in his military career — who is he?
A propertied peasant's daughter who said visions from Saint Margaret and Saint Catherine sent her to lift the siege of Orléans and crown Charles VII — which patron saint of France is this?
Joan of Arc: French folk heroine and saint (1412–1431)
Eldest son of a U.S. Attorney General and older brother of a future Health and Human Services secretary, this Massachusetts congressman founded a nonprofit heating-oil charity in 1979 — who is he?
Joseph P. Kennedy II: American businessman and politician (born 1952)

Also known as the Afrasiabids, this Turkic state ruled Central Asia from the 9th to the early 13th century, conquering Transoxiana and marking a shift from Iranic to Turkic dominance in the region — what was this state called?
Kara-Khanid Khanate: Turkic state in Central Asia from 840 to 1212.

Named by the prophet Mani as one of the four great powers of the 3rd century — alongside Persia, Rome, and China — this African realm was centered on a city in what's now Eritrea and northern Ethiopia. What was it?
Kingdom of Aksum: Polity in Africa and Arabia before 960.
As one of the youngest MPs ever elected to India's Lok Sabha in 1977, he went on to serve as Bihar's chief minister and later as the national railways minister — who is he?
Lalu Prasad Yadav: 20th chief minister of Bihar. Lalu was convicted in the Fodder Scam and was serving a term until 17 April 2021, when he was granted bail by the High Court.
Co-founder of a wrestling promotion that grew into a multinational company, this former Small Business Administration head became the 13th U.S. secretary of education in 2025 — who is she?
Linda McMahon: American administrator and business executive (born 1948)

Born in Atar in French West Africa and a veteran of the Western Sahara War against the Polisario Front, this military officer seized power in a bloodless coup and ruled Mauritania as president from 1984 to 2005 — who is he?
Maaouya Ould Sid'Ahmed Taya: President of Mauritania from 1984 to 2005. Born in Atar, French West Africa, Ould Taya studied at Franco-Arab school and then French military school.
Sparked by a Japanese army claim that a soldier had gone missing near Beijing in July 1937, this three-day clash is considered the start of the Second Sino-Japanese War — what was it?
Marco Polo Bridge incident: Initial battle of the Second Sino-Japanese War.
This Florida congressman, a self-described libertarian populist and Trump ally, filed the 2023 motion that ousted Speaker Kevin McCarthy before resigning in 2024 — who is he?
Matt Gaetz: American politician and TV host (born 1982)
This legendary king of Phrygia was said to turn everything he touched into gold — who was he?
Midas: Phrygian royals, including mythical king with golden touch.
Born in 1950, this Indian activist has served since 2009 as the sixth Sarsanghchalak, or chief, of a major Hindu nationalist organization — who is he?

Serving as Japan's prime minister from 2010 to 2011, this politician was the first in years to hold the post for more than twelve months, and later published a memoir titled 'Fifty Years of Citizen Politics' — who is he?
Naoto Kan: Prime Minister of Japan from 2010 to 2011. On 26 August 2011, Kan announced his resignation.
A Filipino senator and journalist whose 1983 assassination helped topple Marcos and propelled his widow Corazon to the presidency — which opposition leader was he?
This April 1940 assault saw Nazi Germany occupy Denmark within hours and invade Norway on the same morning, launching the Norwegian Campaign — what was this codenamed?
Operation Weserübung: 1940 German invasion of Denmark and Norway in WWII.
Rising from aide-de-camp to Tsar Nicholas II to lieutenant general in World War I, this nobleman seized power in a 1918 coup to become hetman of a short-lived Ukrainian state — who is he?
Pavlo Skoropadsky: Ukrainian and Russian Cossack military and political official; Hetman of Ukraine (1918)
This Odawa war chief led Native Americans against the British in the Great Lakes region from 1763 to 1766, in a conflict that came to bear his name — who was he?
Pontiac (Odawa leader): 18th-century Native American war chief.

She served as France's Minister of Justice under Sarkozy before later becoming Minister of Culture across four different governments, and has been mayor of one of Paris's arrondissements since 2008. Who is this French politician?
Declared independent on a man-made platform in the Adriatic in 1968, this micronation used Esperanto as its official language before being demolished by Italian authorities — what was it called?
Republic of Rose Island: 1968 micronation in the Adriatic Sea. The Italian government viewed it as a ploy by Rosa to raise money from tourists while avoiding national taxation.
This U.S. Army officer led E Company's assault on the Belgian town of Foy after the siege of Bastogne was broken, and later served as the American governor of a Berlin prison — who is he?
Nominated by President George W. Bush in 2005, this jurist became just the second Italian American justice on the Supreme Court, after Antonin Scalia — who is he?
Samuel Alito: US Supreme Court justice since 2006.

Once Adolf Hitler's personal chauffeur and bodyguard, this German officer rose to become the highest-ranking commissioned commander in the Waffen-SS despite having no formal staff training — who is he?
Sepp Dietrich: German Nazi politician and SS commander (1892–1966)

Lasting 872 days and killing an estimated 1.5 million from a prewar population of 3.2 million, this WWII blockade of the Soviet Union's second-largest city was never successfully captured — what was it?
Siege of Leningrad: Blockade by the Axis powers, 1941–1944.

Daughter of Darius III of Persia, she was captured after her father's defeat at Issus and became the second bride of the Macedonian conqueror at the Susa weddings in 324 BC, before being killed by his other spouse, Roxana — who was she?
Stateira (wife of Alexander the Great): Daughter of Darius III, died 323 BC.
A Thai Chinese general, he became the only king of Thonburi after leading the liberation of Siam from Burmese occupation and reuniting a country splintered among warlords — who was he?
Taksin: King of Siam from 1767 to 1782.
One of 24 Apollo astronauts to fly to the Moon, he commanded Apollo 10 and, with his crewmate, became the first to fly a Lunar Module in lunar orbit — which test pilot?
Thomas P. Stafford: American astronaut and lunar explorer (1930–2024)
Dubbed 'the Nelson of the East' by Western reporters, this Imperial Japanese Navy admiral penned Russia's fleet into Port Arthur before a decisive 1905 victory at Tsushima — who is he?

Raiding, trading, and settling from Scandinavia across Europe, North Africa, and even Newfoundland between the late 8th and 11th centuries, this seafaring people helped establish Kievan Rus'. Who were they?
Vikings: Norse seafarers, merchants and raiders.

The first conflict of the Napoleonic Wars, this 1805–1806 struggle pitted Napoleon's France against an alliance of Britain, Austria, Russia, Naples, Sicily, and Sweden, and included the Battle of Trafalgar — which conflict?
War of the Third Coalition: 1805–1806 conflict during the Napoleonic Wars. The Royal Navy, however, assured its naval dominance at the Battle of Trafalgar in October 1805.

Convinced that Protestants and the Catholic majority had to make common cause against the Crown, this revolutionary helped found the Society of United Irishmen in 1791 and became an icon of Irish republicanism — who was he?
Dismembered by the Titans and reborn, this figure from Greek myth was sometimes identified with an Orphic version of Dionysus and linked by Aeschylus to Hades — who is he?
Zagreus: Figure in Greek mythology. In the earliest mention of Zagreus, he is paired with Gaia and called the "highest" god, though perhaps only in reference to the gods of the underworld.
Who among these was born first?
Calouste Gulbenkian (born 1869) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these four was born earliest?
Eratosthenes (born 276 BC) is the earliest of the four.

Messerschmitt Bf 109 (founded 1937) is the earliest of the four. The Messerschmitt Bf 109 is a monoplane fighter aircraft that was designed and initially produced by the German aircraft manufacturer Bayerische Flugzeugwerke (BFW).
Which one below is the oldest?
Lisp (programming language) (published 1958) is the earliest of the four.
Pick the physicist from these four.
Mark Oliphant is a physicist. Born and raised in Adelaide, South Australia, Oliphant graduated from the University of Adelaide in 1922.
Which of these is a chemist?
Karen Silkwood is a chemist. The company settled out of court for US$1.38 million, while not admitting liability.
What is the atomic number of Magnesium?
Magnesium is a chemical element; it has symbol Mg and atomic number 12.
In what year was Josef Mengele born?
Josef Mengele: Before the war, Mengele received doctorates in anthropology and medicine, and he began a career as a researcher.
In what year was Fructose discovered?
Fructose, or fruit sugar, is a common monosaccharide, i.e. a simple sugar.
In what year was Gallium discovered?
Gallium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ga and atomic number 31.

Lorazepam: Pfizer. Lorazepam, sold under the brand name Ativan among others, is a benzodiazepine medication.
Which country is AIDC F-CK-1 Ching-kuo from?
AIDC F-CK-1 Ching-kuo: Taiwan. The aircraft made its first flight in 1989.
Who is credited with discovering Plutonium?
Plutonium: Glenn Theodore Seaborg. Plutonium is a chemical element; it has symbol Pu and atomic number 94.
Who is credited with discovering Fermium?
Fermium: Glenn Theodore Seaborg. Fermium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Fm and atomic number 100.
Who is credited with discovering Sodium?
Sodium: Humphry Davy. Sodium is a chemical element; it has symbol Na (from Neo-Latin natrium) and atomic number 11.
Taken as a pill, cream, or injection, this antiviral medication is the go-to treatment for herpes simplex, chickenpox, and shingles — what is it?
Aciclovir is an antiviral medication. It is primarily used for the treatment of herpes simplex virus infections, chickenpox, and shingles.
This Indian economist won the 1998 Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences for his work on welfare economics and has also studied the causes of famines — who is he?
Amartya Sen (born 3 November 1933) is an Indian economist and philosopher.
This lustrous grey metalloid, found mainly in the mineral stibnite, was historically powdered for use as a cosmetic known by its Arabic name, kohl. What element is it?
Antimony is a chemical element with the symbol Sb (from Latin stibium) and atomic number 51.

Driven mainly by elevated LDL cholesterol, this chronic inflammatory disease quietly builds plaque-filled lesions in artery walls until, often by middle age, it can trigger a stroke or heart trouble — what is it?
Atherosclerosis is a pattern of the disease arteriosclerosis, characterized by development of abnormalities called lesions in walls of arteries.
Native to Southeast Asia, the glossy heart-shaped leaves of this evergreen vine are chewed together with areca nut — name the plant?
Betel (Piper betle) is a species of flowering plant in the pepper family Piperaceae, native to Southeast Asia.
Members of this decapod infraorder tuck a tiny tail-like abdomen under a hard thorax and end their front legs in pincers — which true creatures are they?
Brachyura is an infraorder of decapod crustaceans comprising the true crabs.
This opportunistic yeast lives harmlessly in the gut and mouth of most healthy adults, but can turn pathogenic in immunocompromised people, causing a common fungal infection — what species is it?
Candida albicans is an opportunistic pathogenic yeast that is a common member of the human gut flora.
In calculus, this formula lets you find the derivative of a composed function h(x) = z(y(x)) using the derivatives of z and y separately — what is it called?
Chain rule is a formula that expresses the derivative of the composition of two differentiable functions z and y in terms of the derivatives of z and y.

From a tree in the myrtle family, these dried flower buds from the Moluccas are harvested year-round across different countries and lend their scent to everything from cosmetics to cooking — what are they?
Clove are the aromatic flower buds of a tree in the family Myrtaceae, Syzygium aromaticum.
Released on a daily cycle and spiking when you're stressed, this glucocorticoid raises blood sugar through gluconeogenesis and even tamps down the immune system — what stress hormone is it?
Cortisol is a steroid hormone in the glucocorticoid class of hormones and a stress hormone.
This computer scientist, who died in October 2011, partnered with Ken Thompson to build Unix and also devised the C and B programming languages — who is he?

This hypothetical megastructure would encircle an entire star to capture most of its energy output, conceived as a thought experiment for how an advanced civilization might meet growing power needs — what's the concept called?
Dyson sphere is a hypothetical megastructure that encompasses a star and captures a large percentage of its power output.

Native only to a single island in French Polynesia, this arum-family plant is now one of the world's most popular houseplants, and an ecologically damaging invasive species from South Africa to the Pacific Islands. Name it?
Epipremnum aureum is a species in the arum family Araceae, native to Mo'orea in the Society Islands of French Polynesia.
Which group of vascular plants, which reproduce via spores rather than seeds or flowers, are known for their large megaphyll leaves and the coiled 'fiddleheads' many species unfurl as new growth?
Fern (Polypodiopsida or Polypodiophyta) are a group of vascular plants (land plants with vascular tissues such as xylem and phloem) that reproduce via spores and have neither seeds nor flowers.
Caused by a loss of blood supply, this type of tissue death most commonly affects the feet and hands and can turn skin red or black. What condition is it?
Gangrene is a type of tissue death caused by a lack of blood supply. If the gangrene is caused by an infectious agent, it may present with a fever or sepsis.
This system of rules governs how a language is structured, covering everything from word order to the deeper study of sounds, meaning, and sentence formation — what is it called?
Grammar is the system of rules that governs how a natural language is structured and used, as evidenced by its speakers or writers.
Living to the age of 104, this French pioneer of algebraic topology was also the son-in-law of physicist Pierre Weiss and the eldest of a remarkable scientific brood — who was he?
Henri Cartan (8 July 1904 - 13 August 2008) was a French mathematician who made substantial contributions to algebraic topology.
Classified under sleep-wake disorders in the DSM-5, this condition causes a lack of alertness during waking hours despite — or because of — too much sleep. What is it?
Hypersomnia is a neurological disorder of excessive time spent sleeping or excessive sleepiness.
This medical condition describes a restricted blood supply to tissue or an organ, starving cells of the oxygen they need and often resulting from a blocked or narrowed vessel — what is it called?
Ischemia is a restriction in blood supply to any tissue, muscle group, or organ of the body.
This Confederate veteran and pharmacist sold the rights to his 1886 beverage recipe to Asa Griggs Candler for about $2,300 shortly before he died — who is he?
John Stith Pemberton (July 8, 1831 - August 16, 1888) was an American pharmacist, chemist, and Confederate States Army officer who is best known as the inventor of Coca-Cola.
These paired folds of skin are the major externally visible structures of the vulva, with an outer 'majora' set and an inner 'minora' set — what are they called?
Labia are the major externally visible structures of the vulva. In other mammals, the labia majora are not present and the labia minora are instead referred to as the labia vulvae.
Believed to stem from genetic and hormonal disruption of the lymphatic system, this condition traps fat in the legs regardless of a woman's overall weight — what's the diagnosis?
Lipedema is a condition that is almost exclusively found in women and results in enlargement of both legs due to deposits of fat under the skin.
Transmitted by the bite of Anopheles mosquitoes, this infectious disease causes fever, fatigue, and headaches, and in severe cases can lead to seizures, coma, or death — name the disease?
Malaria is a mosquito-borne infectious disease that is transmitted by the bite of Anopheles mosquitoes.
Crushed leaves of this mint-family herb smell like spearmint, yet it has caused deaths when used as a traditional abortifacient — which species, also known as pennyroyal?

Mentha pulegium (European) pennyroyal, or pennyrile, also called mosquito plant and pudding grass, is a species of flowering plant in the mint family, Lamiaceae, native to Europe, North Africa, and the Middle East.
Also called a mutt, this designation covers any dog outside official breed standards — with an estimated 150 million examples worldwide, believed to enjoy 'hybrid vigor' — what's it called?
Mongrel is any dog which does not belong to one officially recognized breed.

Distinguished from flatworms by having a digestive tract with openings at both ends, these free-living or parasitic roundworms make up their own entire phylum found in nearly every environment on Earth — what are they?
Nematode (or NEEM-; Ancient), roundworms or eelworms constitute the phylum Nematoda.
Many species in this bird family scavenge alongside pigeons and gulls, while two of its city-dwelling members are famous for nesting directly on buildings — which family are they?
Old World sparrow are groups of small passerine birds forming the family Passeridae.
Believed to have originated in Sardinia and cultivated since around the 3rd century BC, this flowering herb native to Greece and North Africa is a kitchen staple worldwide — what is it?
Parsley (Petroselinum crispum), is a species of flowering plant in the family Apiaceae that is native to Greece, the Balkans, Algeria and Morocco.

Left untreated, this inherited metabolic disorder — caused by a faulty gene needed to break down a certain amino acid — can cause intellectual disability, seizures, and a musty body odor — what is it?
Phenylketonuria (PKU) is an inborn error of metabolism that results in decreased metabolism of the amino acid phenylalanine.
This category of polymer includes both natural proteins like wool and silk, and synthetic materials like nylon and aramid fibers — what is it?
Polyamide is a polymer with repeating units linked by amide bonds.
Its biological practitioners link it to neuroscience while its social scientists study groups, all in service of studying the mind and behavior — what is this academic discipline?
Psychology is the scientific study of the mind and behavior. Psychology is an academic discipline of broad scope, crossing the boundaries between the natural and social sciences.

This genus of roughly 60 herbaceous perennials in the buckwheat family includes the familiar pie vegetable prized for its tart stalks despite mildly toxic leaves — which genus, native to Europe and Asia?
Rheum (plant) is a genus of about 60 herbaceous perennial plants in the family Polygonaceae.
This grayish-leaved, purple-flowered evergreen subshrub is a Mediterranean member of the mint family, long used both as a culinary herb and an ornamental garden plant — what plant is it?
Salvia officinalis is a perennial, evergreen subshrub, with woody stems, grayish leaves, and blue to purplish flowers.

This dog breed from southern China, traditionally kept as a property guardian, was driven to the brink of extinction in the 20th century and is known in the West for its deep wrinkles. What breed is this?

Shar Pei (Cantonese; pinyin: sh p) is a dog breed from
southern China.
These eight-legged arachnids inject venom through their fangs and extrude silk from spinnerets, ranking as the largest order in their class — what are they?
Spider (order Araneae) are air-breathing arthropods that have eight limbs, chelicerae with fangs generally able to inject venom, and spinnerets that extrude silk.
A starchy tuber from the morning-glory family, often confused with yams in North America despite being only distantly related to them — what root vegetable is it?
Sweet potato (Ipomoea batatas) is a dicotyledonous plant in the morning glory family, Convolvulaceae.
Raised by a wealthy uncle after his father fled following a fight, this English philosopher laid out an influential social contract theory in his 1651 book 'Leviathan' — who is he?

Thomas Hobbes (HOBZ; 5 April 1588 - 4 December 1679) was an English philosopher and political theorist, best known for his 1651 book Leviathan, in which he expounds an influential formulation of social contract theory.
First isolated as a metal in 1783, this element is drawn from ores like scheelite and wolframite — the latter lending it an alternative name. Which metal is it?
Tungsten (also called wolfram) is a chemical element; it has symbol W (from) and atomic number 74.

Manufactured under license by both Goodyear and Brewster during World War II, this American carrier-based fighter aircraft became one of the most capable fighter-bombers of the war and later saw service in Korea — which aircraft?
Vought F4U Corsair is an American fighter aircraft that saw service primarily in World War II and the Korean War.

Native to freshwater and brackish habitats across western Eurasia, this ray-finned fish in the perch family, related to perch, ruffe, and darters, has become a popular game species well beyond its original range. Name it?
Zander (Sander lucioperca), sander or pikeperch, is a species of ray-finned fish from the family Percidae (which also includes perch, ruffe and darter).
Marked by inadequate cortisol and aldosterone production in the adrenal glands, this rare, long-term endocrine disorder is also known as primary adrenal insufficiency — what is it?
Addison's disease: Endocrine disorder. Addison's disease arises when the adrenal gland does not produce sufficient amounts of the steroid hormones cortisol and (sometimes) aldosterone.
His mother and wife were both deaf, which steered this Scottish-born inventor toward hearing devices — and, in 1876, the first U.S. patent for the telephone. Who was he?
Alexander Graham Bell: Inventor of the telephone (1847–1922)
This inorganic salt, most commonly used as a soil fertilizer, is 21% nitrogen and 24% sulfur by content — what is it?
Useless against the cold, the flu, or any fungus, this kind of medicine works only by killing or stalling bacteria — what is it called?
Antibiotic: Antimicrobial substance active against bacteria.
Dubbed the 'Prophet of the Space Age,' this English science fiction author co-wrote the screenplay for 2001: A Space Odyssey and formed sci-fi's 'Big Three' with Heinlein and Asimov — who is he?
Arthur C. Clarke: British science fiction writer (1917–2008)
With six species native to Africa (and one also found in Arabia), these large Old World monkeys have dog-like muzzles and have existed for at least two million years — what are they called?
Strawberries, blueberries, blackberries, and currants all fall under this small, pulpy, often brightly colored category of fruit — which Britain calls "soft fruit." What is it?
Berry: In the culinary sense, small edible fruit.
Launched in 1993 as a redesigned-wing, glass-cockpit upgrade of an earlier narrow-body jetliner series, this aircraft competes chiefly against the Airbus A320 family — which aircraft is it?
Boeing 737 Next Generation: Single-aisle airliner family.
This volatile red-brown liquid element, with properties between chlorine and iodine, gets its name from the Greek word for 'stench' — which element?
Bromine: Chemical element with atomic number 35 (Br)
Originally defined as the heat needed to raise one milliliter of water by one degree Celsius, this unit of energy in nutrition actually refers to a kilocalorie — what is it?

Calorie: Unit of energy used in nutrition. The small calorie or gram calorie is defined as the amount of heat needed to raise the temperature of one milliliter of water by one degree Celsius (or one kelvin).
Blending science, aesthetics, and technique, this discipline wrestles with projecting a round world onto flat media while deciding what details to keep or cut — what is it called?
Cartography: Study and practice of making maps.
Beyond the resistance-measuring "bridge" that carries his name, this English inventor also gave us the stereoscope, the English concertina, and the Playfair cipher — who was he?
Charles Wheatstone: English physicist and inventor (1802–1875)

Unlike oysters and mussels, which attach to a surface, or scallops, which live near the bottom, this bivalve mollusk instead burrows into sand or mud on the sea floor — what is it, the namesake of a popular chowder?
Clam: Common name for several kinds of bivalve mollusc.

A summer migrant to Europe and Asia that winters in Africa, this bird tricks other species into raising its young by laying eggs that mimic the host's, and even disguises itself as a hawk — what bird is it?
Common cuckoo: Species of bird. It is a brood parasite, which means it lays eggs in the nests of other bird species, particularly of dunnocks, meadow pipits, and reed warblers.

Published in 1750 by a mathematician who described it for any number of unknowns, this linear algebra formula solves systems of equations using determinants of the coefficient matrix — what's it called?
Cramer's rule: Formula for systems of linear equations.
Known as the "grandfather of behavioral economics," this psychologist developed prospect theory with Amos Tversky and won the 2002 Nobel in economics — who was he?
Daniel Kahneman: Israeli-American psychologist and economist (1934–2024)
Named from the Latin word for 'finger' and best known through the common foxglove species, which plant genus produces tall spikes of tubular, often purple flowers?
Digitalis: Genus of flowering plants in the family Plantaginaceae.

Historically nicknamed 'the bloody flux,' this type of gastroenteritis is usually caused by Shigella bacteria or a parasitic amoeba and spreads through contaminated food and water — what is this illness?
Dysentery: Intestinal inflammation causing bloody diarrhea.
Praised by Einstein as the most important woman in the history of mathematics, she proved a theorem linking physical symmetries to conservation laws — who is she?

Comprising more than 700 species mostly native to Australia, these trees and shrubs have oil-gland leaves and a fused 'cap' of sepals and petals covering the stamens, inspiring their Greek-derived name?
This neurodegenerative prion disease has trouble sleeping as its hallmark symptom, most often stemming from a mutation in the PRNP gene — what is it?
Fatal insomnia: Prion disease of the human brain.

Members of this insect order have just one pair of true wings — the hindwings evolved into balance organs called halteres — and the group includes mosquitoes among its 150,000+ species. What are they commonly called?
Fly: Order of insects. A fly (pl. flies) is an insect of the order Diptera (from Ancient Greek δι- di- 'two' and πτερόν pteron 'wing'), named for the single pair of wings.
Capable of living up to 177 years and weighing as much as 417 kilograms, which giant reptile — native to a chain of Pacific islands named for it — is the largest cold-blooded land animal alive today?
Galápagos tortoise: Species of reptile. The species comprises 15 subspecies (12 extant and 3 extinct).
Named from a Latin word for sword, this genus of cormous flowering plants in the iris family is sometimes called the 'sword lily' and is most diverse in South Africa's Cape region — which genus?
Gladiolus: Genus of perennial flowering plants. It is sometimes called the 'sword lily', but is usually called by its generic name (plural gladioli).
Designed specifically for airborne early warning rather than adapted from an existing airframe, this twin-turboprop carrier plane replaced the piston-engined Tracer for the US Navy — which aircraft?
Grumman E-2 Hawkeye: Airborne early warning and control aircraft. The Northrop Grumman E-2 Hawkeye is an American all-weather, carrier-capable, tactical airborne early warning (AEW) aircraft.
Spiny like a porcupine but actually a distant cousin of the shrew, this nocturnal little mammal comes in 17 species across Europe, Asia, and Africa — and was introduced to New Zealand; what is it?

Widely credited as the 'father of the Indian nuclear programme,' this theoretical physicist founded the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research and chaired India's first Atomic Energy Commission — who is it?
Homi J. Bhabha: Indian nuclear physicist (1909–1966)
It usually causes no symptoms at all, yet this persistently elevated arterial pressure is a leading cause of stroke, heart failure and premature death worldwide — what's the medical name for it?
Hypertension: Long-term high blood pressure in the arteries.
This sleep disorder makes it hard to fall or stay asleep, leaving daytime drowsiness, irritability and trouble focusing in its wake — what's its clinical name?
Insomnia: Disorder causing trouble with sleeping.
This U.S. Marine Corps test pilot commanded SpaceX's Crew-7 mission and served as a flight engineer aboard the ISS during Expedition 69/70 — who is she?
Jasmin Moghbeli: NASA astronaut and US Marine Corps officer and test pilot (born 1983)
A 1983 MacArthur Fellow, this American mathematician's work on Hilbert's tenth problem proved crucial to its eventual resolution — now known as the MRDP theorem. Who was she?
Native to southern China and roughly the size of a large olive, which citrus fruit closely resembles a tiny orange and is famously cold-hardy?
Kumquat: Species of small fruit-bearing tree.
Marked by weariness and a desire to act without the energy to do so, which condition can be a normal response to poor sleep or stress, or a sign of underlying illness?
Lethargy: State of tiredness, weariness, fatigue, or lack of energy.
Reaching about 200 kg at its largest, this reddish-brown-shelled reptile ranges through the Atlantic, Pacific, and Indian Oceans as well as the Mediterranean — which species?
Loggerhead sea turtle: Species of marine reptile distributed throughout the world.
A former mayor of Tehran and engineer by training, he served as Iran's sixth president from 2005 to 2013 and championed the country's nuclear program — who is he?

Mahmoud Ahmadinejad: President of Iran from 2005 to 2013. Mahmoud Ahmadinejad (né Sabbaghian; born 28 October 1956) is an Iranian politician who served as the sixth president of Iran from 2005 to 2013.

Born from a US-UK cooperative effort begun in the early 1970s to improve on a first-generation jump jet, this vertical-takeoff-capable attack aircraft has served the US Marine Corps plus Spanish and Italian navies — which aircraft?
McDonnell Douglas AV-8B Harrier II: Anglo-American VSTOL ground-attack aircraft.
Sold under brand names like Ritalin and Concerta, which stimulant medication is preferred as the first-line treatment for ADHD in children, while amphetamine is favored for adults?
Sold under the brand name Provigil, this first-line narcolepsy treatment boosts dopamine without the euphoria or addiction risk of classic stimulants like amphetamine — what is it?
Lacking a cell wall entirely, this genus of bacteria is naturally resistant to beta-lactam antibiotics that target cell-wall synthesis — which genus?
Mycoplasma: Genus of bacteria. Mycoplasma is a genus of bacteria that, like the other members of the class Mollicutes, lack a cell wall (peptidoglycan) around their cell membrane.

Published in the Principia Mathematica, this principle holds that every particle in the cosmos attracts every other with a pull proportional to their masses and inversely proportional to the squared distance between them — which principle is it?
Newton's law of universal gravitation: Classical statement of gravity as force.

This family within the superfamily Delphinoidea includes species with 'whale' in their common names, like the pilot and false killer types, and ranges up in size to the massive orca — what is this family called?
Oceanic dolphin: Family of marine mammals.
This genus of highly sociable ruminants includes domestic sheep, believed to descend from the wild mouflon of central and southwest Asia — which genus?
Ovis: Genus of mammals. Ovis is a genus of mammals, part of the Caprinae subfamily of the ruminant family Bovidae.
This Austrian theoretical physicist, who befriended Einstein in Prague in 1912 and later hosted him often in Leiden, lent his name to a theorem and key work on phase transitions — who was he?
Turning colorless in acid and a fuchsia pink in base, this phthalein dye is a favorite indicator for acid-base titrations — what is it?
Phenolphthalein: pH indicator that turns pink in basic solution.
Its name comes from the Spanish for 'little silver,' yet this dense, stubbornly unreactive metal — element 78 — is so scarce only a few hundred tonnes are mined a year. Which one?
Platinum: Chemical element with atomic number 78 (Pt)

A trained engineer by profession, this royal consort married King Mohammed VI in 2002, becoming the first publicly acknowledged wife of a reigning monarch there to hold an official title, before their discreet 2018 divorce. Who is she?
Princess Lalla Salma of Morocco: Moroccan royal (born 1978)
Imagine a benzene ring with one CH swapped for a nitrogen atom: the result is this flammable, fish-smelling liquid once distilled from coal tar and now made at 20,000 tons a year — what is it?
Known in North America as caribou, this circumpolar deer species ranges from the tiny Svalbard subspecies to the much larger Osborn's version roaming the Arctic tundra — which animal is it?
Reindeer: Species of deer. It is the only representative of the genus Rangifer.

This chronic skin condition causes facial redness, small dilated blood vessels, and in severe cases an enlarged red nose, and can be triggered by spicy food, alcohol, or sun exposure — which condition?
Rosacea: Skin condition, usually on the face.
Nicknamed 'mother-in-law's tongue' and 'snake plant,' this genus of stiff, sword-leaved succulents from Africa and southern Asia is now classified within Dracaena — which genus?
Considered paradoxical by the ancient Greeks in Zeno's puzzle about motion, what term describes an infinite sum of terms added one after another, later made rigorous through the concept of a limit?
Series (mathematics): Infinite sum. In mathematics, a series is, roughly speaking, an addition of infinitely many terms, one after the other.
Coined in the late 18th century, this social science studies human society — from one-on-one interactions to sweeping social structures and everyday culture. What is it?
Sociology: Scientific study of human society and relationships.

Developed in 1962 by an American pharmaceutical company and derived from a natural male hormone, this anabolic steroid treats hereditary angioedema and is unusual for surviving liver metabolism without being esterified — what is it?
Stanozolol: Discontinued steroid for heart treatment.
Among the largest flighted birds in their range, these waterfowl of genus Cygnus typically mate for life and lay three to eight eggs per clutch — what are they?
Swan: Tribe of large water birds.
Element 117 carries the second-highest atomic number of any known element and is named for a U.S. state where key research institutions sit — which element is it?
Tennessine: Chemical element with atomic number 117 (Ts)
Known as linden, lime, or basswood depending on the region, this genus of about 30 tree species is the only one in its plant family to form ectomycorrhizal fungal partnerships. What genus is it?
Tilia: Plant genus. Tilia is a genus of about 30 species of trees or bushes, native throughout most of the temperate Northern Hemisphere.
This essential amino acid, which the body can't make on its own, is a precursor to serotonin, melatonin, and vitamin B3 — which amino acid?
Found in Central and South America, only three living species of this blood-feeding, leaf-nosed flying mammal exist, while two extinct relatives once roamed North America — which creature?

The smallest member of this genus, found in Great Britain, is also considered the tiniest carnivorous mammal species on Earth, with some populations turning white in winter. What group of small predators is this?
Weasel: Mammal of the mustelid family.

Named after a 19th-century British scientist but actually first developed by Leonhard Euler in 1727, this mechanical property measures a solid material's stiffness under tension or compression — what is it called?

Young's modulus: Mechanical property that measures stiffness of a solid material. As such, Young's modulus is similar and proportional to the spring constant in Hooke's law, but with dimensions of pressure instead of force per distance.

Thulium is denoted by which symbol?
The symbol for thulium is Tm. Thulium is a chemical element; it has symbol Tm and atomic number 69.

Dwayne Johnson: Dwayne Douglas Johnson (born May 2, 1972), also known by his ring name "The Rock", is an American actor and professional wrestler.
In what year was Jude Law born?
Jude Law: David Jude Heyworth Law (born 29 December 1972) is an English actor.
